correctness.rationale: For every odd n>=3 and exactly three zeros, the proof reduces equal-half zero counts to j=0 or 1. For j=1, the chosen consecutive zero pair gives necessary-and-sufficient integer start bounds floor(g/2)+1<=m<=min(K,g+min(j,h)-1). After sorting a<=b<=c, the intermediate interval is contained in the small-gap interval; the large-gap interval reaches K. Their union and the longest all-ones run give N=K-1_{c even}+max(0,min(K,a+b-1,floor(c/2))-floor(a/2)). The sole even-c baseline deficit m=c/2 is compensated no later than m=c/2, proving EVERY prefix inequality, including n=3 and adjacent zero boundaries. A fresh independent enumerator compared exact types and all prefixes for 1,036 words of odd length 3..15. These finite checks corroborate but do not replace the interval proof.

value.rationale: This gives a motivated infinite subfamily of a recent explicitly open prefix-count conjecture, with a complete per-half-length type spectrum and closed three-gap formula, not a finite-table improvement. The distinction between circular and linear factors is structurally important; the result does not claim the unrestricted conjecture.

limitations: Only odd n and exactly three marked letters, not arbitrary binary circles or four-marker families.
Fresh finite checks corroborate 1,036 cases; mathematical infinitude follows from proof, not checker.
